items.t: Main streets: Marine Drive along the waterfront; Caulfeild Drive, Keith Road and Headland Drive inside the neighbourhood; and the Upper Levels Highway across the north side. Caulfeild Village Centre is the area's shopping centre.

There are no condo buildings in Caulfeild; West Vancouver's condos are in Ambleside and Dundarave, to the east. The former Caulfeild Land Use Contract area is now zoned CD86 (Caulfeild Zone), and in its Residential Area A, buildings and land can't be stratified, so no strata homes can be built in that part of the neighbourhood.

Transit anchors: TransLink route 253 (Caulfeild Village / Park Royal), operated as West Vancouver Blue Bus, runs via Caulfeild Drive, Cherbourg Drive, Keith Road and Marine Drive, with select trips continuing to Vancouver via the Lions Gate Bridge; route 262 runs Caulfeild Village to Horseshoe Bay, Lions Bay and Brunswick Beach; route 250 runs on Marine Drive. The area's main exchange is Park Royal.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Caulfeild

items.t: Zoning and plans: West Vancouver's Zoning Bylaw No. 4662 (2010) and Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 4985, 2018). The former Caulfeild Land Use Contract area is now CD86 (Caulfeild Zone, 2024): Residential Area A allows up to three units per lot and no strata. Nearby RS single-family zones have minimum site areas from 488 m² (RS5) to 8,094 m² (RS1).

Heritage: Lower Caulfeild is a designated Heritage Conservation Area, planned by Francis Caulfeild from 1899; owners within the area need a Heritage Alteration Permit for any work — this applies to the Caulfeild Cove area lots as much as to detached houses, and any strata exterior work plan runs through it.

Hazard permit areas: the District applies an Environmental Development Permit Area for watercourses (work within 15 metres of the top of a watercourse bank), a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit Area (within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface) and a Foreshore Development Permit Area for coastal hazards — all three can apply in Caulfeild, the foreshore area on Lower Caulfeild waterfront lots.

West Vancouver property taxes: 2026 taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on unpaid current taxes on July 2, 2026 and a further 5% on outstanding current taxes on September 2, 2026. At Caulfeild price points the Province's additional school tax can also apply — 0.2% on the residential portion of assessed value between $3 million and $4 million and 0.4% above $4 million for 2026, rising to 0.3% and 0.6% on January 1, 2027.

blocks.text: Good to know about Caulfeild condos

items.t: The zoning explains why there are no condos. Caulfeild's former Land Use Contract was replaced by CD86 zoning in 2024 (Amendment Bylaw No. 5321, 2024), and CD86 Residential Area A prohibits stratification. So the lack of condos comes from the bylaw, and it won't change without a rezoning.

Caulfeild Cove is a 1970s complex in a much older neighbourhood. The townhouses were built in 1974, wood frame, in a neighbourhood whose Lower Caulfeild subdivision was planned from 1899 and is now a designated Heritage Conservation Area. Price it on its depreciation report, not on the area's estate homes.

The foreshore is a permit area, not just a view. Lower Caulfeild waterfront lots sit in the Foreshore Development Permit Area for coastal hazards, and Caulfeild Park's washrooms are open 7 a.m. to 9 p.m., May through October, under a Caulfeild Park Management Plan — the park at the neighbourhood's south edge is managed as an environmental and heritage site, not a simple beach park.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Caulfeild

items.t: Fee-simple homes (the homes around it): Caulfeild is in the District of West Vancouver, and the District's bylaws apply.

Zoning and plans: West Vancouver's Zoning Bylaw No. 4662 (2010) and Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 4985, 2018), which names the Caulfeild Village Centre. The former Caulfeild Land Use Contract area is now zoned CD86 (Caulfeild Zone, 2024), with two residential areas, a commercial area and parks. In Residential Area A, the minimum lot is the lot as registered, each lot can have up to three units, and strata isn't allowed. Nearby RS single-family zones have minimum site areas of 8,094 m² in RS1, 1,625 m² in RS2, 975 m² in RS3, 731 m² in RS4 and 488 m² in RS5.

Heritage and hazard permit areas: Lower Caulfeild is a designated Heritage Conservation Area — Francis Caulfeild planned and designed the subdivision from 1899 to control the character of later development, and owners within the area need a Heritage Alteration Permit for any work, which any strata exterior-work plan at Caulfeild Cove runs through as well. The District also applies an Environmental Development Permit Area for watercourses (work within 15 metres of the top of a watercourse bank), a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit Area (within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface) and a Foreshore Development Permit Area for coastal hazards — all three can apply in Caulfeild, the foreshore area on Lower Caulfeild waterfront lots.

District tax timing and additional school tax: District of West Vancouver 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty applied to unpaid current taxes on July 2, 2026 and a further 5% on outstanding current taxes on September 2, 2026; approximately 50% of the tax bill is collected by the District and remitted to other taxing authorities. At Caulfeild price points the Province's additional school tax can also apply — 0.2% on the residential portion of assessed value between $3 million and $4 million and 0.4% above $4 million for 2026, rising to 0.3% and 0.6% on January 1, 2027. West Vancouver water and sewer utilities are metered and billed quarterly by the District.

blocks.text: Good to know about Caulfeild townhomes

items.t: The zoning itself explains the missing townhouses. Caulfeild's former Land Use Contract was replaced by CD86 zoning in 2024 (Amendment Bylaw No. 5321, 2024), and CD86 Residential Area A prohibits stratification — so Caulfeild Cove standing alone is a bylaw outcome, not a market accident, and it will not change without a rezoning.

The District's heritage walk starts at the complex's cove. The District's Caulfeild heritage walk notes Caulfeild Cove and the municipal dock where pilot boats were moored, and St. Francis-in-the-Wood church — the "Cove" in the complex's name is the historic pilot-boat cove two blocks from the strata.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Caulfeild
Fee-simple lots

items.t: CD86 lots (the former Land Use Contract area): this area is now zoned CD86 (Caulfeild Zone) under a 2024 amendment, with two residential areas, a commercial area and parks. Each lot's minimum size is simply its registered size (no new minimum applies), and Residential Area A allows up to three units per lot. A fee-simple lot has no strata, Form B or strata fees.

Nearby RS lots: minimum site areas are 8,094 m² in RS1, 1,625 m² in RS2, 975 m² in RS3, 731 m² in RS4 and 488 m² in RS5. These are minimums, not actual lot sizes; check a specific lot on the District's Zoning Map.

Heritage-shaped lots (Lower Caulfeild): Lower Caulfeild is a designated Heritage Conservation Area; the District states Francis Caulfeild planned and designed the subdivision from 1899 to control the character of later development, and owners within the area need a Heritage Alteration Permit for any work. The 1899 plan is the subdivision fabric of Lower Caulfeild — its lots are heritage-regulated fee-simple lots, not a current lot offering.
Serviced vs unserviced: West Vancouver water and sewer utilities are metered and billed quarterly by the District — the serviced position for District lots as the District states it.

Hazard-shaped land: all three District permit areas can apply in Caulfeild — the Foreshore Development Permit Area on Lower Caulfeild waterfront lots, the Wildfire Hazard Development Permit Area (within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface), and the Environmental Development Permit Area (within 15 metres of the top of a watercourse bank). Gross lot area is not buildable area here.

blocks.text: Development change

items.t: The CD86 rezoning itself (Amendment Bylaw No. 5321, 2024): is the area's most recent District-significant land-use change: it replaced the former Land Use Contract with conventional zoning. It created no lot offering.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and transit near Caulfeild lots

items.t: Municipality: District of West Vancouver, BC — Caulfeild is the District's western neighbourhood, with Lower Caulfeild at the foreshore, Upper Caulfeild north toward Highway 1, Lighthouse Park to the west and Marine Drive along the south.

Name status: the District uses the name Caulfeild on its neighbourhood context map and in OCP Bylaw No. 4985, 2018 policy for the Caulfeild Village Centre, one of the District's village centres alongside Dundarave and Horseshoe Bay. No street-by-street written boundary is published by the District. Note the spelling: the District and SD45 use "Caulfeild" (with the second "u"), not "Caulfield."
Nearby areas: Lighthouse Park (west), Altamont and West Bay (east), Cypress Park Estates (north, across Highway 1) and the Marine Drive waterfront (south).

Roads and transit: Marine Drive along the waterfront, Caulfeild Drive, Keith Road and Headland Drive inside the neighbourhood, and the Upper Levels Highway across the north side. Blue Bus route 253 (Caulfeild Village / Park Royal) runs via Caulfeild Drive, Cherbourg Drive, Keith Road and Marine Drive, with some trips continuing to Vancouver over the Lions Gate Bridge; route 262 runs from Caulfeild Village to Horseshoe Bay, Lions Bay and Brunswick Beach; and route 250 runs on Marine Drive.

Parks and services: Caulfeild Park offers the Caulfeild Trail, rocky foreshore, sandy beaches and swimming in calm, protected water; Lighthouse Park, at the west edge, has trails through old-growth forest to the historic lighthouse. Caulfeild Village Centre is the commercial centre named for the area in OCP Policy 2.3.4. The West Vancouver Community Centre and Aquatic Centre, 2121 Marine Drive in Ambleside, and West Vancouver Memorial Library, 1950 Marine Drive, serve Caulfeild. Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street, North Vancouver, serves the North Shore.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Caulfeild

items.t: Zoning and plans: West Vancouver's Zoning Bylaw No. 4662 (2010), including CD86 (Caulfeild Zone, 2024) for the former Land Use Contract area and the RS zones nearby, and the Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 4985, 2018), which names the Caulfeild Village Centre.

The stratification bar (CD86 Residential Area A): stratification of buildings or land is prohibited under Amendment Bylaw No. 5321, 2024. Added units in Residential Area A (maximum three dwelling units per lot) therefore cannot be sold as separate strata lots — suite and coach-house value there is rental/family value on one fee-simple title, never strata-lot value. District building-permit guidance addresses secondary suite and detached secondary suite (coach house) applications in the single-family areas around CD86.

How many homes per lot outside CD86, under the zoning bylaw: a maximum of 4 homes per lot, or 6 if any part of the site is within 400 metres of a designated bus stop. Inside CD86, the CD86 rules above apply, so don't price a CD86 lot on the District-wide figure.

Heritage Alteration Permit (Lower Caulfeild): any work inside the designated Heritage Conservation Area needs a Heritage Alteration Permit, on top of ordinary permits — flag it up front rather than letting it surface at subject removal.

Hazard development permits: an Environmental Development Permit is required for work within 15 metres of the top of any watercourse bank; a Wildfire Hazard Development Permit is required for work within the Wildfire Hazard Development Permit Area, described as within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface; a Foreshore Development Permit is required for work within the Foreshore Development Permit Area (waterfront property or property at risk of coastal flooding), which applies on Lower Caulfeild waterfront lots.

Strata rules: check the Form B (fees, amounts owing, levies, contingency reserve balance and insurance; within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page). Stratas with 5 or more lots need a depreciation report every 5 years, and at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve. Rental bans are void, so a directory's "rentals not allowed" line for Caulfeild Cove doesn't apply to long-term rentals. Only 55+ age bylaws are valid, so a "45+" listing line isn't enforceable.

I don't know of any ALR land in Caulfeild. On ALR land, homes can't be stratified, subdividing needs Agricultural Land Commission approval, the main house can be up to 500 m² with a suite only inside it, and an additional home can be up to 90 m² (40 ha or less) or 186 m² (larger). Farm tax status needs farm income of $10,000 on under 0.8 ha, $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha, or $2,500 plus 5% of the land value over 4 ha, with applications due by October 31.

blocks.text: Good to know about Caulfeild lots

items.t: The subdivision is from 1899, and it still governs: Francis Caulfeild planned and designed the Lower Caulfeild subdivision from 1899 specifically to control the character of later development — the Heritage Conservation Area and its Alteration Permit are that plan still operating, which is why Lower Caulfeild lots carry a permit layer no other West Vancouver lot carries in the same way.

The Land Use Contract is gone — old listing language is stale: any Caulfeild document still describing the area as governed by a Land Use Contract predates Amendment Bylaw No. 5321, 2024, which replaced the contract with CD86 zoning (Residential Areas A and B, a Commercial Area and a Parks and Greenspaces Area). Underwrite suite and density questions off CD86, not the contract.

The spelling is a search trap: the District and SD45 use "Caulfeild" (second "u"); a comp search run only under "Caulfield" misses District documents and school material, and a search run only under the correct spelling can miss misspelled listings.

Three permit areas overlap at the west end of the District: the foreshore at the water, wildfire near the forest toward Lighthouse Park, and watercourse setbacks inland. Caulfeild is the one area where all three of the District's permit areas can apply to ordinary house lots.

No market figure exists to quote for this neighbourhood: West Vancouver is outside SnapStats coverage entirely, so any Caulfeild median, ratio or trend figure attributed to SnapStats anywhere should be treated as an error.
